text.p: Turkish treasury heavily sold 11-month bills in an auction on Tuesday with Wednesday settlement, in line with previous expectations, bankers said.
They said strong sales emerged in the bond market after the the auction which is expected to raise cash demand sharply on Wednesday.

The treasury sold 280 trillion lira nominal-valued bills having June 10, 1998 maturity at 120.37 percent yield (including witholding tax), compared to 229.1 trillion lira of 10-month bills it sold at 125.08 percent in last Tuesday's auction.
Banks will pay 134.3 trillion lira to the Treasury for the auction on Wednesday and also pay 47.7 trillion lira to the central bank for maturing open market repos.

"Panic selling which came after the auction in the bond market due to expected cash squeeze can be stopped by the central bank's funding (via open market). The bank is expected to open a new repo auction on Wednesday to relieve the shortage," a private banker said.
The newly sold June 10, 1998 bills were heavily sold with Wednesday settlement after the auction and its yield rose to 104.84 percent from the auction yield of 104 percent, excluding witholding tax.

Bond trade was subdued before the auction, but yields firmed by around 1.5-2 percentage points on banks' paper sales ahead of the auction and expectations of higher inflation following 15-32 percent price rises in petroleum products announced on Monday, bankers said.
The most heavily traded papers were May 13, 1998 and April 1, 1998, yielding 104.26 and 103.68 percent, respectively, up 1.62 and 1.57 percentage points from Monday.

The central bank drained 10.3 trillion lira at 52 percent overnight after the market opened 74 trillion lira long but lent 6.5 trillion lira at 71 percent via tom/next due to expected liquidity shortage for Wednesday.

The average overnight money rate fell to 55.19 percent from Monday's 61.19. The average overnight repo was little changed at 65.62 percent versus 65.14 percent due to the central bank's support, bankers said.
They said the bank stepped in briefly to buy overnight repos at 65 percent during the day.
The Turkish lira weakened sharply to 153,800 to the dollar from Monday's close of 153,350 in line with a sharp rise in the dollar/mark parity.
